requirements.REQ_PROVIDER: Real Terraform Plugin Framework provider exposes exactly the ten documented managed resources with the stable documented attribute interfaces.
requirements.REQ_STATE: Terraform Core owns durable state and stable identities derive from external object keys rather than mutable desired attributes.
requirements.REQ_REFRESH: Read observes native Linux state without Ansible side effects and makes external drift actionable.
requirements.REQ_UPDATE: Create/Update publish new state only after successful mutation; failed updates preserve the last successful state and retries converge.
requirements.REQ_DELETE: Delete completes only after successful scoped teardown or confirmed absence; failures retain management and sibling ownership is preserved.
requirements.REQ_COPY: Copy/template use source intent, observe destination state, and manage documented metadata.
requirements.REQ_TEXT: Named line/block resources implement regexp/marker semantics, remain idempotent, side-effect-free on Read and independently owned.
requirements.REQ_IDENTITY: User/group and named text/cron resources observe native state and preserve stable identity across mutable changes.
requirements.REQ_RUNNER: Runner uses structured argv, propagates non-zero/timeout/cancellation failures, cleans ephemeral playbooks on every terminal path, and does not persist command output in Terraform state.
requirements.REQ_NORMALIZE: Equivalent modes, unordered values, supplementary groups and cron defaults converge to stable canonical representations.
requirements.REQ_CRON: Cron omitted/explicit defaults converge, external drift is reconciled, schedules update in place and named siblings are preserved.
requirements.REQ_OWNERSHIP: Only one Terraform resource may own a given path, user, group, or user-plus-cron-name external object key.
requirements.REQ_BACKEND: Create, Update and Delete use Ansible across resource families while clean Read/refresh uses native observation only.
